tagline.text: A 40-hectare safari park in Clark Freeport with tigers and bears

location.label: Location
location.text: 67 Jose Abad Santos Avenue, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–April dry season (December–February is most comfortable)

children.text: Opened in December 2021 inside the Clark Freeport Zone, this safari-style zoo covers about 40 hectares. One ticket lets you see more than 1,500 animals of over 70 species, including tigers, lions, bears and crocodiles, which makes it a good outing for families with children.

Clark Safari and Adventure Park is a zoo and safari park in the Clark Freeport Zone in Mabalacat City, Pampanga. During development it was also introduced as "Clark Safari and Rainforest Adventure Park," while most booking sites and map apps today use the name "Clark Safari and Adventure Park." It is the same place, so try both names when searching. Owner Romy Sitchon invested about ₱135 million to build it. Construction began in 2019, was delayed by the COVID lockdowns, and the park opened to the public on
December 8, 2021
The grounds cover about
40 hectares

and are said to hold more than 1,500 animals of around 70 species. Around the lagoon near the entrance stand life-size statues of African giants such as elephants, hippos, rhinos and gorillas, which make popular photo spots. Keep in mind that these are only statues and there are no live animals of those species, so you won't be disappointed. The live animals are mainly big cats and predators such as Bengal tigers, white tigers, white lions, leopards, jaguars, black panthers, wolves and hyenas, plus brown and black bears, primates such as baboons and macaques, reptiles such as crocodiles and pythons, and birds such as pelicans, hornbills and macaws.

One ticket covers most of the animal zones, while feeding, young-animal encounters, horse riding and safari truck rides cost extra. The walking routes are long and have uphill sections, so if you travel with children or older relatives it is wise to use the safari truck as well. A review from 2022, in the park's early days, noted unfinished areas and a lagoon without water, so treat the facilities as a work in progress and check recent reviews before you go.

Even within Clark the park sits toward the edge, so walking to other attractions is not practical. Many visitors combine it with Clark city, the restaurant strips of Angeles and nearby theme parks such as Aqua Planet and Dinosaurs Island for a full day. It is only 2–3 hours by car from Manila, so it also fits easily into a half day on your first or last day after arriving at Clark airport.

Life-size statues of elephants, hippos, rhinos and gorillas ring the lagoon just inside the entrance, making it a good place for your first souvenir photo. They are not live animals, so save the safari feeling for the zones further in. Photos come out best in the soft morning light.

This zone, home to Bengal tigers, white tigers, white lions, leopards, jaguars, black panthers, wolves and hyenas, is the park's biggest attraction. Most of the animals sleep in the shade at midday, so you are more likely to see them moving early in the morning or after 3 PM.
Here you will find brown bears, black bears, baboons, macaques and a liger, a cross between a lion and a tiger. Visitors report that bananas for the bears can be bought at a stall for around
, and children love this feeding the most. Feeding is allowed only during designated sessions.

Get up close to reptiles such as saltwater crocodiles, pythons, tortoises and monitor lizards. Many visitors say the area is kept clean and does not smell bad, and there are paid photo sessions with some reptiles and parrots.

blocks.title: Rin's Petting Zoo and Kids Spot

children.text: This children's area lets you meet and feed herbivores such as goats, sheep, zebras and deer, along with farm animals. Visitors report that fish food and farm animal food cost around
each. There is also a playground and a garden, so it is a nice place for kids to rest.

You can see pelicans, hornbills, macaws, peacocks and birds of prey, and there is a photo booth for pictures with birds. Photos with birds are generally listed at a few dozen pesos per bird, but check the exact price on site.
The viewing trail up the hill lets you see crocodiles, wolves, wild dogs and deer, and families who find walking hard can take the safari truck. The group truck tour lasts about
2 hours
with a guide and is listed at about
for 10–15 people.
The park says that cultural performances by the Aeta indigenous community are held from time to time. The schedule is not fixed, so ask at the information counter when you enter what is on today.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: See the animals in the morning and have lunch inside the park

children.text: Arrive when the gates open and confirm your ticket at the welcome center. If you have an online booking voucher such as one from Klook, you can enter with the voucher without queuing at the ticket booth.
Take photos at the statues around the lagoon, then head to Kingdom Panthera first, while the animals are most active in the morning.
Visit Bear Kingdom, the primate zone and Reptile Kingdom in turn. If bear feeding is offered, do it at this time.
Feed the animals with the kids at Rin's Petting Zoo and Kids Spot, then take photos at the aviary photo booth.
Have a Filipino lunch at Banua Restaurant. A boodle fight spread for 4–5 people is listed at about
Finish up before the heat peaks and head back in a car you arranged in advance. The park is on the outskirts and rides are scarce, so secure your transport before you leave.
Plan on 2–5 hours in total. Right after opening, 8–11 AM, and after 3 PM are the times with fewer people and more active animals.

items.title: Clark full-day route
items.subtitle: Combine the safari with Clark city

children.text: Spend the morning at Clark Safari.
Have lunch inside the park or at a restaurant in Clark city.
Move on to another Clark attraction or a shopping mall to rest or try a light activity. Calling a Grab or a taxi is the easiest way to get around.
Have dinner at a night market or restaurant district in Clark city, then return to Manila or your hotel.
For Clark city, see the Clark entry (
Clark
) in the same region for more details.

items.title: From Manila by car or rental car

children.text: From Manila, take NLEX northbound, switch to SCTEX and exit at Clark South Interchange (Exit 91). The trip takes about
2–3 hours
from Manila.
From the interchange, follow Prince Balagtas Avenue and Claro M. Recto Highway straight to the park. Tolls are listed at about ₱350–400 one way, so check the latest rates.
Parking is listed as free.
Hiring a car with a driver for the day to tour Clark together is popular with families.
Take a Victory Liner or Five Star bus from Cubao or Pasay and get off at the Dau Terminal in Mabalacat. The ride takes about
2 hours 15 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
From the Dau Terminal, transfer to a Grab or taxi for about
30 minutes
at roughly ₱340–420.
After landing at Clark International Airport (CRK), take a Grab or taxi to the park inside Clark Freeport. It is close, so you can make a short trip of it.
You can also take a Genesis P2P bus from NAIA Terminal 3 or Trinoma to Clark International Airport or SM City Clark, then switch to a Grab or taxi.
In Clark and Angeles, Grab and Blue Taxi are the easiest ways to get around, and tricycles can cover short distances.
The park is on the edge of Clark, so it can be hard to get a ride around closing time. Decide on your ride back before you enter.
Much of the visit is spent walking outdoors, so the dry season is far more comfortable. December–February is described as relatively cool and clear, the most pleasant time.
Animals often rest in the shade during the hottest hours, so in any season it is best to go right after opening or late in the day. Weekdays are quieter than weekends.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Most comfortable and good for long walks. Crowded on weekends and holidays
Go early in the morning; a hat and water are essential. Avoid midday
Afternoon showers are common, so mornings work better. Bring an umbrella

Inside the park there is Banua Restaurant, which serves Filipino dishes and snacks, as well as food trucks and a fast-food area near the entrance. Reviews from the opening period said food choices were limited and the restaurant opened later, so decide in advance whether you will eat inside the park. Outside food and drinks are listed as not allowed.

You stay in Clark or Angeles rather than inside the park. There are many resorts and hotels in Clark city and many hotels and guesthouses around Walking Street in Angeles, with restaurants ranging from Korean and Filipino to Western food. For a family trip, staying on the Clark side keeps the ride to the safari short.
Online vouchers such as Klook are about ₱400 cheaper than the gate price, so book before you leave. Vouchers are valid for 180 days but are non-refundable.
Right after opening, between
and
, or after 3 PM, there are fewer people and the animals are more active. Weekdays are quieter.
The routes are long with uphill sections, so bring comfortable shoes, a hat, sunscreen, a compact umbrella and a power bank. The midday heat is intense.
Feeding activities and horse riding may require cash, so bring small bills.
If you travel with children or older relatives, using the safari truck saves energy.
Decide on your ride back before you enter. The park is on the outskirts and it is hard to get a Grab around closing time.
The elephants, hippos, rhinos and gorillas are statues, not live animals. Setting your expectations accordingly means less disappointment.
Hours, prices and open zones can change, so check the latest notices on the park's official Facebook page or a booking site before you visit.
For the animals' welfare and your safety, do not feed animals outside designated sessions, tap on the enclosure glass or lean over the fences.
Drones and loud Bluetooth speakers are listed as prohibited. Check the rules on site.
Reviews give the last admission time as anywhere from 4 PM to 5:30 PM, so it is safest to arrive before 3 PM at the latest.
Some reviews mentioned areas under construction, a lagoon without water and many sleeping animals. Facilities and animal activity can vary greatly from day to day.
The heat and the uphill sections tire children and older visitors easily. Drink plenty of water and rest often in the shade.
Ticket prices and ID discount conditions may change, so check the latest notices on site.
The central area of the Clark Freeport Zone where the park is located, with malls, casinos, restaurant districts and a night market, making it a good place to rest before or after the safari.
A water park facility inside the same Clark Freeport, often paired with the safari for a family itinerary. It is within driving distance.
A family attraction in Clark themed around dinosaur models, often suggested as a same-day combination with the safari.
An amusement park near Clark that can fit into the same day if you travel with children who like rides.
